kb.q: how to use orcid analyse profile
kb.a: Enter an ORCID (format: 0000-0000-0000-0000) in the analysis form on the home page to see the full profile along with the SDG distribution of the publications.

kb.q: what is orcid researcher id number
kb.a: ORCID is an international unique researcher identifier in the form 0000-0000-0000-0000. The platform uses it to pull publication data automatically.
Open the Researchers page to search by name or institution, or type an ORCID straight into the analysis form on the home page.

kb.q: how to use doi analyse article
kb.a: Enter an article DOI (for example 10.1234/example) in the analysis form to see its SDG classification, impact metrics and citations.

kb.q: what is doi digital object identifier
kb.a: A DOI (Digital Object Identifier) is a unique identifier for a scholarly article. The usual form is 10.xxxx/… Use a DOI to open an article profile on this platform.
Open the Articles page to search by title, author or year. You can also use the DOI form on the home page for a direct analysis.

kb.q: what are sdgs sustainable development goals
kb.a: The SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) are the 17 goals set by the UN to be reached by 2030. This platform maps research onto those 17 goals.
Open the Analytics or SDGs Cluster page to explore how research is distributed across the 17 SDGs.
In the platform's data, SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 4 (Quality Education) and SDG 3 (Good Health) are the most researched. See the Analytics page for the full picture.
SDG 13 (Climate Action) is one of the fastest-growing research topics on this platform. Related articles are on the SDGs Cluster page.
Open the Journals page for the list of indexed journals, with quartile, impact factor and SDG distribution.
Filter journals by quartile (Q1–Q4) on the Journals page. Q1 journals carry the highest impact factor in their category.
Open the Institutions page for partner universities and research bodies, together with their researcher and publication statistics.
The Trends Analysis page shows how SDG research has developed over time, based on publication data from 2019 onwards.
The Analytics page holds the full picture: SDG distribution, yearly trends and impact metrics across all research on the platform.
The Leaderboard page ranks researchers by Wizdam Impact Score (WIS), citations and publication output.
The Wizdam Impact Score (WIS) is a composite metric combining a researcher's academic, social and economic impact together with their SDG contribution.
The AI Insights feature on the home page reads the research data automatically and surfaces relevant findings and trends from the platform's article collection.
Open the Register page to create a Sciecola account. A researcher account gives you a personal dashboard and your own SDG contribution statistics.
Open the Login page to sign in to your Sciecola account.
Use "Forgot password" on the Login page to reset it through your registered email address.
Once signed in, your personal dashboard shows a summary of your activity, saved articles and SDG contribution statistics.
The full API documentation is on the Docs page. The Sciecola API lets you pull SDG data into your own research system or institutional platform.
Open the Help or Contact page for technical support. The Sciecola team answers through the contact form.
The FAQ page under Docs answers common questions about using the platform, reading the data, and access policy.
Sciecola is an AI-based research analytics platform that maps scholarly publications onto the 17 UN SDGs, built to serve the Indonesian and global research communities.
